title: From Facts to Personas: Interpretable Role Unlearning in LLMs via Mixture-of-Experts
abstract: arXiv:2611.19393v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLMs are widely adopted in multi-role dialogue and persona simulation. However, their strong ability to imitate role-specific linguistic and behavioral patterns can introduce privacy risks, reinforce social biases, and lead to unsafe or uncontrollable outputs. To address these issues, we introduce the Role-playing Unlearning task, which aims to selectively forget the style and knowledge associated with target roles while preserving the language ability and behaviors of the remaining roles. Unlike prior unlearning tasks that focus solely on removing factual information, our task additionally requires forgetting persona-specific characteristics, making the control over model generation more fine-grained. We propose RoleMoE, a Mixture-of-Experts framework that maps different roles to more independent expert subspaces, improving role separation and structural interpretability. translated_abstract: 大语言模型已被广泛应用于多角色对话和角色人格模拟。然而，其强大的模仿特定角色语言和行为模式的能力可能带来隐私风险、强化社会偏见，并导致不安全或不可控的输出。为解决这些问题，我们提出了“角色扮演遗忘”任务，旨在选择性地遗忘与目标角色相关的风格和知识，同时保留其余角色的语言能力和行为。与以往仅专注于删除事实信息的遗忘任务不同，我们的任务还要求遗忘角色特有的个性化特征，从而使对模型生成的控制更加细粒度。我们提出了RoleMoE，一个混合专家框架，它将不同角色映射到更加独立的专家子空间，提升了角色分离度和结构可解释性。为进一步区分角色特有特征，RoleMoE引入了
tldr: 该论文提出RoleMoE混合专家框架，通过将不同角色映射到独立的专家子空间，实现大语言模型中细粒度、可解释的角色扮演遗忘——选择性遗忘目标角色的风格与个性化特征，同时保留其余角色的语言能力。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes RoleMoE, a Mixture-of-Experts framework that maps roles to independent expert subspaces, enabling fine-grained and interpretable role unlearning in LLMs—selectively forgetting target personas' style and knowledge while preserving the capabilities of remaining roles.
